grammar_rules.title: Present Tense - Regular Verbs (A1)
grammar_rules.explanation: In Dutch, you conjugate verbs by adding endings to the stem of the verb. You get the stem by removing -en from the infinitive (whole verb).
key_points: Note: in questions, 'jij' doesn't get extra -t

questions.question: Conjugation of 'maken' (to make): Ik ... elke dag huiswerk.
questions.explanation: For 'ik' use only the stem: maak (maken - en = maak)

questions.question: Conjugation of 'wonen' (to live): Hij ... in Utrecht.
questions.explanation: For 'hij' use stem + t: woon + t = woont

questions.question: Conjugation of 'studeren' (to study): Wij ... aan de universiteit.
questions.explanation: For 'wij' use the whole verb: studeren

questions.question: Conjugation of 'spelen' (to play): Jij ... voetbal.
questions.explanation: For 'jij' use stem + t: speel + t = speelt

questions.question: How do you ask 'Do you work?' in Dutch?
questions.explanation: Werk jij? - In questions with 'jij', the verb doesn't get an extra -t

grammar_rules.title: Perfect Tense - Regular Verbs (B1)
grammar_rules.explanation: The perfect tense in Dutch is used to express completed actions in the past. It is formed using the auxiliary verb 'hebben' or 'zijn' + the past participle.
key_points: Use 'zijn' for movement verbs and state changes
Regular verbs follow the t-kofschip rule

questions.question: Complete: 'Ik ___ gisteren naar de film ___' (I went to the movie yesterday)
questions.explanation: Use 'ben' because 'gaan' is a movement verb, and the past participle is 'gegaan'

questions.question: Complete: 'Zij ___ hard ___' (She has worked hard)
questions.explanation: Use 'heeft' because 'werken' is not a movement verb, and the past participle is 'gewerkt'

questions.question: What is the past participle of 'maken' (to make)?
questions.explanation: The past participle is 'gemaakt' (ge + maak + t)

questions.question: What is the past participle of 'komen' (to come)?
questions.explanation: The past participle is 'gekomen' (ge + kom + en)

questions.question: Complete: 'Wij ___ naar Amsterdam ___' (We have traveled to Amsterdam)
questions.explanation: Use 'zijn' because 'reizen' is a movement verb, and the past participle is 'gereisd'

grammar_rules.title: Irregular Verbs - Common Patterns (A1)
grammar_rules.explanation: Some Dutch verbs have irregular conjugations in the present tense. These verbs don't follow the standard stem + ending pattern.
key_points: Some verbs have vowel changes in the stem
Common irregular verbs: zijn, hebben, gaan, komen, doen

questions.question: Conjugation of 'zijn' (to be): Ik ___ een student.
questions.explanation: Ik ben - 'zijn' is irregular, 'ik' form is 'ben'

questions.question: Conjugation of 'hebben' (to have): Hij ___ een boek.
questions.explanation: Hij heeft - 'hebben' is irregular, 'hij' form is 'heeft'

questions.question: Conjugation of 'gaan' (to go): Wij ___ naar huis.
questions.explanation: Wij gaan - 'gaan' is irregular, 'wij' form is 'gaan'

questions.question: Conjugation of 'komen' (to come): Zij ___ uit Nederland.
questions.explanation: Zij komen - 'komen' is irregular, 'zij' form is 'komen'

questions.question: Conjugation of 'doen' (to do): Ik ___ mijn huiswerk.
questions.explanation: Ik doe - 'doen' is irregular, 'ik' form is 'doe'

grammar_rules.title: Past Tense - Regular Verbs (A2)
grammar_rules.explanation: The past tense (imperfect) in Dutch is used to describe actions that happened in the past. Regular verbs follow the t-kofschip rule for the past tense.
key_points: Past tense uses different endings than present
Follow the t-kofschip rule for regular verbs
Learn common irregular past tense forms

questions.question: Past tense of 'werken' (to work): Ik ___ gisteren.
questions.explanation: Ik werkte - past tense adds -te to the stem

questions.question: Past tense of 'wonen' (to live): Hij ___ in Utrecht.
questions.explanation: Hij woonde - past tense adds -de to the stem

questions.question: Past tense of 'studeren' (to study): Wij ___ hard.
questions.explanation: Wij studeerden - past tense adds -den to the stem

questions.question: Past tense of 'spelen' (to play): Zij ___ voetbal.
questions.explanation: Zij speelde - past tense adds -de to the stem

questions.question: Past tense of 'koken' (to cook): Jullie ___ samen.
questions.explanation: Jullie kookten - past tense adds -ten to the stem

grammar_rules.title: Nouns and Articles (A1)
grammar_rules.explanation: Dutch nouns have gender (masculine, feminine, or neuter) which determines which article to use. The articles are 'de' (common gender) and 'het' (neuter gender).
key_points: Learn the gender with each noun

questions.question: Which article is correct: '___ boek' (the book)?
questions.explanation: Het boek - 'boek' is a neuter noun

questions.question: Which article is correct: '___ vrouw' (the woman)?
questions.explanation: De vrouw - 'vrouw' is a feminine noun

questions.question: Which article is correct: '___ kinderen' (the children)?
questions.explanation: De kinderen - plural nouns always use 'de'

questions.question: Which article is correct: '___ water' (the water)?
questions.explanation: Het water - 'water' is a neuter noun

questions.question: Which article is correct: '___ auto' (the car)?
questions.explanation: De auto - 'auto' is a common gender noun

grammar_rules.title: Adjectives - Basic Patterns (A2)
grammar_rules.explanation: Dutch adjectives change form depending on whether they come before a noun and what article is used. They can be inflected (with -e) or uninflected (no ending).

examples.dutch: De auto is groot (the car is big)

questions.question: Complete: 'De ___ auto' (the red car)
questions.explanation: De rode auto - adjective gets -e before 'de' noun

questions.question: Complete: 'Het ___ boek' (the new book)
questions.explanation: Het nieuwe boek - adjective gets -e before 'het' noun

questions.question: Complete: 'De auto is ___' (the car is old)
questions.explanation: De auto is oud - no ending after verb

questions.question: Complete: 'De ___ huizen' (the small houses)
questions.explanation: De kleine huizen - adjective gets -e for plural

questions.question: Complete: 'Het ___ kind' (the happy child)
questions.explanation: Het blije kind - adjective gets -e before 'het' noun
